domain_label: Equipment Placement, Route Setup & Consumables Logistics
purpose: A verifiable operating method for converting a won office-coffee-and-water account into a serviceable placement and keeping it serviceable: surveying the breakroom and its water, matching brewer and water-system classes to measured consumption, executing an install that satisfies locally verified plumbing and sanitation obligation classes, designing a consumables catalog and honest par from observed draw-down, and then setting the service cadence, territory, sequence, truck load and maintenance regime that constitute the route cost engine of the business.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
the operator places and retains ownership of the brewing and water equipment at the client site and earns recurring revenue from consumables and service, rather than selling machines outright
service is delivered by a physical route: a stocked vehicle, a driver, and a repeating weekly pattern of stops inside a bounded geography

sanitation, food-handling, plumbing and trade-licensing requirements vary by country, state, municipality and building; each is treated as an obligation class to verify locally and is never asserted here as a specific current rule

consumption rates, service minutes, filter life, failure rates and route costs are account-specific quantities to be measured or derived from a stated mechanism, never taken from an invented industry number
exclusions: finding, qualifying and winning the account - office segments by headcount and culture, the free-trial and tasting acquisition play, displacement of self-serve retail buying, and proposal design across placement, rental and purchase models - which belongs to the OCS market-targeting and account-acquisition knowledge base

stop-level profitability analysis, consumables pricing and repricing, retention programs, expansion into snacks, breakroom supplies and micro-market class upgrades, route-density growth economics and account-book valuation, which belong to the route-economics, retention and expansion knowledge base

invented figures for route cost, consumption per person, equipment price, filter life or failure rate; every such quantity appears only as a mechanism with a stated way to measure or verify it for the specific account

asserting any specific health-permit, food-handler, plumbing-code, backflow or trade-licensing requirement as current fact; this knowledge base names the obligation class and requires dated local verification
personalized legal, tax, financial or insurance advice, including advice on equipment financing structures, depreciation treatment or coverage selection

any stocking practice not grounded in measured consumption and client agreement, including overstocking a client to inflate a delivery, leaving unrequested product to be billed later, or pressuring a site contact into accepting more than the room uses
facilities management of the client's own kitchen, dishwashing, catering or food service beyond the placed beverage equipment, its consumables and its cleaning

competency_questions.question: What exactly counts as a completed placement, and when is an account genuinely installed and serving rather than still in setup?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PLACEMENT_MANDATE states the done-state and the ownership boundary of placed equipment, and INSTALL_EXECUTION_HANDOVER supplies the handover evidence that proves the done-state was reached

competency_questions.question: What do I have to measure in the breakroom before I promise any equipment or a service day?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SITE_SURVEY enumerates the measurements (space, power, water, drain, storage, access path, contact) and marks which findings block an install

competency_questions.question: How do I work out how much coffee and water this office will actually consume, without guessing and without talking the client into more than the room drinks?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONSUMPTION_PROFILE gives the estimation mechanism with sourced input bands and the first-cycle measurement that replaces it, and HONEST_STOCKING_ETHICS binds every proposed quantity to measured draw-down and client agreement

competency_questions.question: Which class of brewer fits this office's peak demand and this room, and what does choosing the wrong class cost me on the route?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BREWER_CLASS_SELECTION maps demand, footprint, power, water, cleaning minutes, consumable format and spare availability onto a machine class and names the route cost of a mismatch

competency_questions.question: Bottled cooler or plumbed bottleless, and what does this building's water force me to install?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: WATER_QUALITY_AND_FILTRATION converts a dated test of the actual supply point into a filtration class and change interval, and WATER_SYSTEM_SELECTION weighs bottle-exchange labour against plumbed install and building permission

competency_questions.question: What must be true before install day - water tap, drainage, circuit, leak containment - and which sanitation and trade-licensing obligation classes apply to me, my drivers and this building?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PLUMBING_AND_POWER_SETUP lists the utility readiness conditions and the licensed-trade boundary, and SANITATION_OBLIGATION_CLASS names each obligation class with the authority to verify it locally and the documentation to retain

competency_questions.question: What should the consumables catalog contain, and how do I set a par that keeps the room stocked without stuffing a closet full of product nobody asked for?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONSUMABLES_CATALOG_DESIGN defines the shared core and variable tail of the SKU set, PAR_LEVEL_DESIGN derives par from cycle length, measured draw-down, storage cap and freshness window, and HONEST_STOCKING_ETHICS supplies the disclosure and reduction rules

competency_questions.question: How often should this account be serviced, and what actually drives that cadence?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SERVICE_CADENCE_DESIGN derives cycle length from draw-down, storage capacity and freshness, states the exception rule for emergency stops, and treats cadence as the primary route cost dial

competency_questions.question: How do I lay out a territory and sequence a day so drive time and locked doors do not eat the route?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ROUTE_TERRITORY_DESIGN clusters accounts into repeating day zones with interleaved cadence classes, and ROUTE_SEQUENCE_TIME_WINDOWS sequences the day inside access windows, dock and parking constraints

competency_questions.question: What goes on the van each morning, and how do I stop the truck and warehouse becoming a sink of stale product and unexplained shrink?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: VEHICLE_LOAD_TRUCK_INVENTORY defines pick lists, buffer sizing and end-of-day reconciliation, WAREHOUSE_REPLENISHMENT sets reorder points against lead time and freshness, and PRODUCT_ROTATION_FRESHNESS gives the date-code and rotation discipline across depot, van and client shelf

competency_questions.question: What cleaning and preventive maintenance keeps the equipment alive and the cup drinkable, and when do I repair at the counter versus swap the machine out?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CLEANING_PM_CADENCE ties each task and interval to water condition, throughput and the sanitation obligation class, and EQUIPMENT_RELIABILITY_SWAP gives the triage rule, spare-pool sizing mechanism and failure log

competency_questions.question: Where is every machine I own right now, and how do I get it back when an account ends?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ASSET_REGISTER_RECOVERY defines the serialized register, its status states, and the de-install and refurbishment path that returns a unit to the spare pool

competency_questions.question: What must the driver do and record at every stop so par and cadence can be retuned and the stop can be judged downstream?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: ROUTE_DRIVER_STANDARD defines the standard stop, the required training classes and the no-inflation conduct boundary, and SERVICE_RECORD_HANDOFF specifies the per-stop fields and the handoff to stop-level economics

glossary.definition: The trade of placing beverage equipment in workplaces and supplying it on a recurring route; the operator owns the equipment, the client owns the room, and the money is in consumables and service rather than hardware.
One breakroom served by named, serialized equipment with an agreed stock plan and a scheduled service cadence; the unit of delivery this knowledge base builds and maintains.
The quantity of a given consumable that should be on the client's shelf when the driver leaves, derived from cycle length, measured draw-down, storage capacity and the product's freshness window.
The measured quantity of a consumable actually taken from the client's shelf between two service stops; the only honest basis for par, cadence and equipment sizing once the first cycles are complete.

A water dispenser plumbed into the building supply with its own filtration stages instead of fed by exchanged bottles; trades bottle-handling labour for install work, building permission and filter-change service.
Pre-portioned ground coffee sized to one batch of a specific brewer; format compatibility between fractional packs, pods and whole bean is what locks a machine class to a catalog line.

The interval between scheduled stops at an account - weekly, biweekly, monthly or on a named exception - and the single largest cost dial in route operations because it multiplies across every account on the book.

The split of a route day between productive minutes inside accounts and unproductive minutes in the vehicle, elevator or lobby; territory design and sequencing exist to move minutes from the second bucket to the first.

The reserve of bench-ready units held per machine class so a failed unit can be swapped rather than repaired on the counter; sized as a mechanism from placements of that class, observed failure rate and bench turnaround time.

The category of device or arrangement - an air gap, a check-valve assembly or a specified backflow preventer - required so water drawn into placed equipment cannot flow back into the building's potable supply; which class applies to a given machine and building is an obligation to verify locally with the plumbing authority and the property manager, never assumed from a previous site.

nodes.definition: Fix the operating unit this subdomain delivers. A placement is one breakroom served by named, serialized equipment, an agreed stock plan and a scheduled service cadence, where the machine remains the operator's capital on loan rather than hardware the client bought. The mandate defines what installed and serving means - equipment brewing to spec on the client's own water, filters fitted and dated, consumables at agreed par, a real route day assigned, a named site contact and escalation path, and the serial recorded in the asset register - and it states the standing promise the route exists to keep: the room does not run out and the machine works. Every downstream decision about sizing, install, par, cadence and truck load is judged against this done-state, and a signed account with no completed placement is a cost centre, not revenue.

included: the definition of a placement and its done-state checklist
the ownership boundary of placed equipment versus client premises
the standing service promise and named escalation contact
excluded: winning the account, trial offers and proposal or rental-model design
stop-level profitability, pricing and account-book value

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a pattern of early service calls traced back to accounts that were switched on without a completed done-state checklist

pros.claim: A hard done-state stops half-finished accounts being counted as live while quietly generating service calls
pros.example: a brewer sitting on a counter with no filter fitted and no assigned route day is still in setup, not on the service book

cons.claim: A strict done-state delays go-live and can frustrate a client who wants coffee the next morning
cons.example: holding the start of service because the water test result and the lockable stock cabinet are both outstanding

failure_modes: counting a delivered machine as a completed placement and discovering later that nobody was assigned to service it
leaving ownership of the equipment ambiguous so retrieval is contested when the account ends
no named site contact, so every jammed brewer routes back to the salesperson instead of the route
acceptance_tests: every account marked live carries a serialized asset entry, a stocked par, an assigned route day and a named site contact with an escalation path
revisit_triggers: the client moves, adds a floor, or splits one breakroom into two
the service model at the account changes, for example a second brewer or a water system added to an existing coffee placement

nodes.definition: Before any equipment touches a breakroom, identify which classes of obligation attach to handling food-contact product and equipment on other people's premises: food-handler or food-safety training classes that may apply to route staff, health-department registration or inspection classes that some jurisdictions extend to brewed and vended beverage service, potable-water and backflow-protection classes for plumbed equipment, food-contact surface and sanitizer handling rules, labelling and allergen rules where product is repackaged, and the building's or tenant's own layered requirements such as insurance certificates and vendor badging. This unit produces a local obligation register that names each class, the authority that owns it, the documentation the business must be able to produce on request and the date each was verified. Every threshold, fee, interval or permit name is flagged verify current rules in your jurisdiction rather than asserted, because these rules differ by country, state, county, city and building.

included: obligation classes and the authority to verify each with
training classes for route staff and the records retained
building and tenant vendor requirements layered on public rules
excluded: asserting any jurisdiction's current specific rule, fee or permit as fact
legal advice
the client's own kitchen and dishwashing hygiene obligations

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a dated answer from the health, water or licensing authority, or a building adding a vendor requirement, that changes what the register says is required

pros.claim: Naming the obligation class before install prevents a placement being unwound by an inspection or a building rule discovered afterwards
pros.example: learning at survey time that plumbed equipment in that tower must be connected by a licensed trade with documented backflow protection

cons.claim: Verification burns calendar time and sometimes fees before any revenue exists, and answers can be slow or ambiguous
cons.example: waiting on a county environmental-health answer about whether route drivers servicing brewers need a food-handler card

failure_modes: assuming the rule from the neighbouring county or the operator's home city applies in the new one
repackaging bulk coffee or creamer into unlabelled containers for delivery
letting a driver's training card or the company's insurance certificate lapse unnoticed until a building refuses access
acceptance_tests: the obligation register names each applicable class, the authority contacted, the verification date and the document held, and no specific requirement is relied on without a dated local verification
revisit_triggers: the route expands into a new city, county or state
a renewal date, rule-change notice or building vendor-policy update arrives

nodes.definition: Walk the actual breakrooms before promising anything, and capture with numbers and photographs the constraints that decide every later choice: how many people are on site on a typical day and on which floors, how many break areas exist and where, free counter depth and linear space, the nearest cold-water supply and whether a serviceable shutoff exists, drain access, which electrical circuit serves the counter and what already shares it, the volume of cabinet or closet space available for stock and whether it locks, the delivery path from kerb to counter including dock, freight elevator, stairs, badge, escort and permitted delivery hours, and the site contact who genuinely controls the room. The survey is a measurement exercise, not a conversation: nearly every later dispute about the machine not fitting, the breaker tripping or the driver not getting in before nine traces back to a survey line that was never taken.

included: measured space, power, water, drain and storage findings per room
the delivery and access path with its time constraints
identification of the site contact and blocking findings
excluded: choosing the equipment class, which happens after consumption and water are known
negotiating the commercial terms of the account

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: install-day surprises or aborted stops that a survey line should have caught, indicating the survey checklist is missing a field

pros.claim: Measured constraints prevent a second trip with the wrong machine and give an honest install date
pros.example: finding that the only free counter outlet shares a circuit with a microwave before specifying a high-draw batch brewer

cons.claim: A proper survey costs an unbilled visit and slows the momentum of a client who has just said yes
cons.example: a multi-floor tenant requiring three separate escorted walks before anything can be specified

failure_modes: surveying one floor and assuming the other break areas match it
accepting the client's headcount claim instead of counting desks, badges or observed cup use
not photographing the under-counter plumbing and then guessing at the tap point on install day
acceptance_tests: the survey record carries per-room measurements, power and water findings, storage volume, the access path with its hours, photographs, and an explicit list of findings that block installation
revisit_triggers: the office remodels, moves, or reassigns the breakroom
headcount or the on-site-days policy changes materially

nodes.definition: Turn headcount into an evidence-backed expectation of what the room will actually pull, then replace that expectation with measurement as quickly as possible. The mechanism, stated as a mechanism rather than a number: on-site headcount times the share who drink each category times cups per drinker per day times days on site, split across the drink mix of brewed coffee, single-cup, tea, hot chocolate and drinking water, then adjusted for visitor and meeting traffic, hours the office is occupied, and whether the staff currently buy their own coffee retail or from a nearby shop. Every input is recorded as a band with its evidence source - client statement, desk or badge count, an observed cup station, a photographed shelf - and the opening cycles exist to convert those bands into observed draw-down per SKU. Estimates seed the opening stock only; from the first measured cycle onward, draw-down governs par, cadence and equipment sizing.

included: the estimation mechanism with sourced input bands
the drink-mix split and visitor and meeting allowance
conversion of the estimate into measured draw-down over the first cycles
excluded: consumption potential used to qualify or price a prospect before it is won
revenue or margin projections built on consumption

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: measured draw-down from completed cycles diverging from the estimate, or a change in the office's on-site pattern

pros.claim: An explicit mechanism makes the estimate auditable and correctable instead of a salesperson's hunch
pros.example: showing the client the assumption of three on-site days and revising it when they say the office is empty on Fridays

cons.claim: Early cycles carry genuine error, so the room can be under-served or over-supplied before the profile settles
cons.example: a launch week inflated by an all-hands meeting that makes steady-state demand look far higher than it is

failure_modes: treating total employees as on-site headcount in a hybrid office
ignoring visitor and meeting-room draw in a client-facing floor
anchoring par to the first week rather than to a full measured cycle
acceptance_tests: every input band names its evidence source, and the profile is re-derived from measured draw-down after the first full cycles with the variance against the estimate recorded
revisit_triggers: a hybrid or return-to-office policy change alters on-site days
headcount shifts, a floor is added or given up, or the drink mix visibly changes

nodes.definition: Test the building's water at the exact point the equipment will draw from, before choosing filtration, because water is simultaneously the product and the main enemy of the equipment. Capture hardness, dissolved solids, chlorine or chloramine taste and odour, visible sediment, and any building-side treatment already in line such as a softener or a whole-building filter. Map those readings onto a filtration class: sediment pre-filtration, carbon for taste and odour, scale inhibition or softening where hardness is high, and finer treatment classes where the client's expectations or the equipment's tolerance demand it. Filter capacity is a mechanism - rated throughput volume degraded by water condition - so the change interval is derived from measured usage and the test result rather than from a calendar habit, and the same readings set the descale interval that the maintenance plan inherits.

included: testing the actual supply point and recording the result with a date
mapping readings onto a filtration class and stage order
deriving filter and descale intervals from throughput and water condition
excluded: choosing between bottled and plumbed delivery, which is the water-system decision
asserting a regulatory water-quality standard as current fact

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a retest, a plumbing change in the building, or scale findings on service that contradict the current interval

pros.claim: Matching filter class to measured water protects both cup quality and the machine's heater and valves
pros.example: catching high hardness on an upper-floor tenant fed by an old riser and specifying scale inhibition before the first brew

cons.claim: Testing adds a step and a cost, and building water varies by riser, floor and season so one sample can mislead
cons.example: sampling the janitor's utility tap rather than the kitchen line the brewer will actually be plumbed into

failure_modes: sampling the wrong tap and specifying filtration for water the machine will never see
using a calendar filter interval that ignores how much water the account actually pulls
assuming a municipal water report describes the condition at the tap after the building's own plumbing
acceptance_tests: a dated test from the actual supply point is on file with the derived filter class, stage order and a change interval expressed as a function of measured throughput
revisit_triggers: the municipal source, seasonal blend or building treatment changes
descale findings or filter-life observations start disagreeing with the derived interval

nodes.definition: Choose the class of brewing equipment the demand profile and the room can actually support: single-cup pod systems for small or low-volume rooms and for offices that want variety, single-cup with a hot-water bypass where tea and instant demand exists, thermal batch brewers with satellite servers for volume rooms where a queue forms at nine, airpot or urn setups for meeting-heavy floors, and bean-to-cup grinders where the client will notice quality and tolerate a cleaning regime. The selection variables are peak throughput and recovery time against counter footprint, the power and water the survey found, cleaning minutes per cycle, the consumable format the machine locks the account into, and how many spare units of that class the operation can hold. Machine class is a route-cost decision wearing an equipment costume: each class carries its own service minutes, failure profile, spare requirement and stocking pattern, and every additional class in the fleet fragments training, parts and truck space.

included: matching class to peak demand, recovery time and room constraints
consumable-format compatibility and spare-pool implications
fleet standardization discipline
excluded: whether the client rents, buys or receives the equipment on placement terms
water system choice and filtration class

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: measured peak-hour behaviour, service-minute logs or class-level failure history that contradicts the sizing assumption

pros.claim: Matching class to peak demand keeps the morning queue moving without over-capitalizing a small room
pros.example: a batch brewer with a second satellite server on a shift-change floor where a single-cup machine would stall at eight forty-five

cons.claim: Every additional class in the fleet fragments spares, training and truck stock, so the best machine for one room can be the worst for the route
cons.example: placing one bean-to-cup unit that needs its own burr-cleaning routine, its own parts and a dedicated spare

failure_modes: specifying to impress the client rather than to serve measured demand
ignoring recovery time so the machine is technically adequate but empty at peak
introducing a one-off class with no spare unit and no trained driver
acceptance_tests: the specified class is justified in writing against peak-hour demand, footprint, power and water, cleaning minutes and spare availability, and uses a consumable format the catalog already carries
revisit_triggers: measured draw-down moves the account up or down a demand band
the reliability log shows a failure pattern concentrated in this class

nodes.definition: Decide how the account receives drinking water: bottled coolers, which carry a recurring exchange labour and a storage burden for full and empty bottles, or plumbed point-of-use bottleless systems, which carry an install, a filtration service obligation, building permission and a leak exposure - and, where the room warrants it, a combination unit that also feeds hot water or the brewer. The decision weighs measured water draw against the labour of moving bottles through a lobby and freight elevator, the client's storage for full and empty stock, the building's willingness to permit a line tap and the conditions it attaches, hot-tank safety in a shared breakroom, and the different failure and service profiles of each option. Recurring economics enter only as mechanisms - exchange minutes per stop, filter change interval by throughput, install effort amortized over the expected placement life - never as invented figures.

included: bottled versus plumbed decision variables and their labour and service profiles
building permission and storage constraints
hot-tank and dispense safety considerations at placement
excluded: the price the client is charged for water service
specific plumbing execution, which is the utility setup unit

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a building permission decision, or bottle-handling minutes recorded on the route that change the labour comparison

pros.claim: A plumbed system removes recurring bottle labour and storage, which is often the largest hidden cost of a water account
pros.example: an account on the ninth floor of a building whose freight elevator must be booked, where bottle exchange consumes more stop time than the coffee service

cons.claim: Plumbed systems introduce install dependency, building permission risk and a standing leak exposure that bottles never have
cons.example: a tenant whose landlord refuses any new tap into the riser, stranding a plumbed proposal after the survey

failure_modes: specifying a plumbed unit before confirming the building will permit the tap
underestimating bottle storage so full and empty bottles colonize the client's corridor
ignoring hot-tank safety in a breakroom used by the public or by children at a family-visit day
acceptance_tests: the chosen system is justified against measured water draw, the access and storage findings, and a documented building permission or an explicit bottled fallback
revisit_triggers: building management changes its policy on line taps or vendor plumbing work
measured water draw moves far enough that the labour comparison flips

nodes.definition: Prepare the utilities the placement will live on, and decide who is permitted to do that work. This covers the water tap itself - a proper tee and a serviceable shutoff rather than a self-piercing saddle, line material and routing that will not be crushed by a drawer, adequate pressure at the point of use - the backflow or air-gap protection class the equipment and the building require, drainage where the equipment needs it, leak containment such as a drip pan and a shutoff the client's facilities team can reach, and an electrical circuit that carries the machine's draw without sharing with a microwave or a toaster oven. It also fixes the licensing boundary: which parts of this work may be performed by the operator's technician and which require a licensed plumbing or electrical trade, verified for the jurisdiction and for the building's own vendor rules. This is the highest-consequence unit in the subdomain because a slow leak inside a tenant's casework can cost more than the account will ever earn.

included: tap method, shutoff, line routing and pressure verification
backflow or air-gap protection class and drainage
circuit adequacy and the licensed-trade boundary verified locally
excluded: performing or advising on work that requires a licensed trade in that jurisdiction
the client's building-wide plumbing beyond the connection point

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a leak or electrical incident at any placement, or a change in the local trade-licensing or building vendor rules

pros.claim: A serviceable tap with its own shutoff turns every future filter change and swap into a short, low-risk task
pros.example: a filter change completed in minutes because the technician can isolate the line at the counter instead of hunting the building shutoff

cons.claim: Doing the work properly costs install time, sometimes a licensed trade, and can push the go-live date
cons.example: waiting for a building-approved plumber to fit a tee and shutoff instead of piercing the supply line the same afternoon

failure_modes: using a piercing saddle valve that clogs and later weeps behind the cabinet
sharing a circuit with a high-draw appliance so the breaker trips every morning
skipping leak containment and a reachable shutoff at a tenant whose facilities team has no way to stop a flow
acceptance_tests: the connection is pressure-tested and inspected dry after a soak period, the shutoff and containment are documented with photographs, the circuit is verified under load, and any work requiring a licensed trade carries that trade's record
revisit_triggers: any leak, weep or breaker trip reported at the account
the building changes its vendor or trade-licensing requirements

nodes.definition: Execute the install day so the room works from the first cup and the client knows what to do. The sequence: stage equipment and stock, flush new lines and filters until the water runs clean, brew to specification and taste-check on the client's own water with the brew volume and ratio calibrated for the equipment, sanitize food-contact parts, and lay out the station so traffic flows - cups and condiments off the brew path, waste and recycling adjacent, spill and burn risk minimized, the stock location secured and labelled. Then hand over: walk the client's people through daily use and the two or three things that break machines, label the equipment with the service contact, agree the escalation path and the service day, and capture a sign-off recording serial numbers, filters fitted with dates, opening par and the named contact. The handover record, not the delivery, is what closes the placement.

included: flush, calibration, sanitizing and brew-to-spec verification
station layout, waste placement and secured stock location
client walkthrough, escalation path and signed handover record
excluded: the commercial agreement and its terms
the maintenance schedule beyond the first filter and PM dates recorded at handover

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: early-life service calls or client complaints that map back to a step the handover checklist does not cover

pros.claim: A calibrated brew and a five-minute walkthrough remove most of the avoidable early service calls
pros.example: showing the office manager how to reseat the brew basket so a weekly jam never becomes an emergency stop

cons.claim: A thorough install consumes a long slot in a route day and often needs a second person
cons.example: an install that runs past noon and pushes two scheduled service stops into the following day

failure_modes: skipping the line and filter flush so the first pots taste of carbon fines
leaving the station arranged so the queue blocks the microwave and the client rearranges it badly
no signed record, so serials, filter dates and opening par are reconstructed from memory later
acceptance_tests: the handover record shows flushed lines, a calibrated and tasted brew, sanitized contact surfaces, photographed layout, serials and filter dates, opening par, the named contact and the agreed service day
revisit_triggers: the client rearranges or relocates the station
early service calls cluster on issues the walkthrough was supposed to prevent

nodes.definition: Treat every placed machine as capital on loan and keep a register that can answer, at any moment, where it is and what has been done to it: serial, class, install date, account and specific room, filter and descale history, accumulated service events, and a status of placed, spare, on the bench, or retired. The same unit owns the end of the placement: scheduling a de-install, safely capping or removing the water connection, recovering the machine and any unopened stock, cleaning and refurbishing the unit back into the spare pool or writing it off with a reason, and updating the register the same day. It also fixes what the client is told at placement about who owns the equipment and how access for retrieval works, so a cancellation does not become an argument about a machine bolted into someone else's counter.

included: the serialized register, its fields and status states
de-install, recovery, refurbishment and write-off procedure
the ownership and access understanding recorded at placement
excluded: depreciation, tax treatment and financing of the equipment
why the account ended and how to save it

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a physical audit of placed and spare equipment that disagrees with the register

pros.claim: A live register makes recovery routine and lets maintenance history follow the machine rather than the account
pros.example: seeing that a recovered unit was already descaled twice at its last placement before it goes back out

cons.claim: Register discipline adds a data step to every install, swap and recovery, and it decays quickly when skipped
cons.example: a driver swapping two units between accounts on a busy morning and never updating the entries

failure_modes: machines that exist in the ledger but cannot be located at any known account
de-installing without capping or documenting the water connection
recovering equipment without recovering the unopened stock, which is then written off silently
acceptance_tests: every serial reconciles to a status and a location, and each de-install closes with a dated recovery record covering the machine, the water connection and any returned stock
revisit_triggers: a physical audit finds a serial where the register did not expect it
a cancellation notice starts the retrieval clock

nodes.definition: Design the set of items the operation will actually carry: coffee by format matched to the placed machines - fractional packs sized to each batch brewer, pods for single-cup, whole bean for grinders - across a small number of roast and profile tiers, plus decaf, tea, hot chocolate, creamers in their liquid, powder and refrigerated forms, sugar and substitutes, stirrers, cups and lids by size, filters, sanitizer and cleaning chemicals, and water cups. The discipline is subtraction: every SKU added multiplies warehouse slots, truck space, count time, dead-stock exposure and the chance of a mis-pick, so the catalog is a deliberately short shared core that most accounts draw from, plus a small variable tail for genuine account-specific requests, and no format enters the catalog unless a placed machine class uses it.

included: the shared core and variable tail SKU architecture
format compatibility with placed machine classes
rules for admitting and retiring a SKU
excluded: what each item is priced at or repriced to
snack, breakroom-supply and micro-market assortment expansion

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: slow-moving or orphaned SKUs surfacing in cycle counts, or a fleet class change that strands a format

pros.claim: A short shared core makes pick lists fast, counts honest and substitution easy when a supplier is short
pros.example: one house roast in a single fractional-pack size covering most batch-brewer accounts on the route

cons.claim: A narrow catalog cannot satisfy every taste request and can read as inflexible to a client who wants their own blend
cons.example: an account asking for a specialty single-origin that no other stop on the route uses

failure_modes: admitting a SKU for one account and carrying it for years after that account leaves
stocking a coffee format no placed machine can brew
letting near-duplicate items proliferate so counts and pick lists become unreliable
acceptance_tests: every catalog line maps to at least one placed machine format or a standing account requirement, and each variable-tail SKU carries an owning account and a review date
revisit_triggers: a machine class is retired from the fleet, orphaning its format
a supplier discontinues or reformulates a core line

nodes.definition: Set, per account and per item, the quantity that should be on the client's shelf when the driver leaves. The derivation is explicit: cycle length times measured draw-down, plus a safety allowance sized to how painful a stock-out of that item is and how variable the room's demand is, capped by the storage volume the survey found and by the freshness window of the product. Par is a living number, seeded from the consumption profile and then reset from the last cycles' actual draw-down, with every reset logged and its reason recorded. It is the single lever that decides both stock-outs and the quiet resentment of a closet stacked with product nobody asked for, and it is also the input the truck load and the cadence are built from, so a sloppy par propagates into every cost line on the route.

included: the par derivation and its storage and freshness caps
safety allowance sizing by stock-out pain and demand variability
logged par resets from observed draw-down
excluded: what the delivered quantity is billed at
using par as a sales target or a quota

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: logged stock-outs, aged product on the client's shelf, or a measured draw-down shift that the current par no longer matches

pros.claim: A par derived from measured draw-down and real storage keeps the room supplied at the lowest inventory the client has to house
pros.example: cutting a creamer par after two cycles show the room draws far less than the opening estimate assumed

cons.claim: Par requires per-account maintenance, and a stale par is worse than none because it is trusted
cons.example: an account still stocked for a full floor months after half the team moved to another building

failure_modes: setting par from the estimate and never resetting it from measured draw-down
ignoring the storage cap so product ends up stacked on the floor of a copy room
raising par to reduce stop frequency without telling the client
acceptance_tests: each account's par sheet shows, per item, the cycle length, the measured draw-down it was derived from, the storage and freshness caps applied, and the date and reason of the last reset
revisit_triggers: a stock-out or an aged-product finding is logged at the account
the consumption profile changes after a headcount or on-site-days shift

nodes.definition: Bind the whole stocking operation to what the room actually consumes and to what the client has knowingly agreed. The standing rules: quantities are proposed from measured draw-down, never from a delivery target; any increase in par or in a delivered quantity is disclosed and agreed with the site contact before it ships; product the client did not request is not left behind to be billed; slow-moving items are removed from the account rather than topped up cycle after cycle; the client can see what was delivered and what was on the shelf beforehand; drivers are never compensated or pressured in a way that rewards leaving more product than the room uses; and a request to reduce, pause or remove an item is honoured on the next cycle without friction. The same rules apply to water, filters and any breakroom item the route carries. This is a first-class operating constraint on par, cadence and truck load, not a courtesy.

included: disclosure and agreement before any quantity increase
removal of slow-moving items and honouring reduction requests
the no-inflation rule for driver conduct and incentives
excluded: price fairness and repricing conversations
acquisition-stage promises and trial-offer conduct

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: client complaints about quantity, aged stock accumulating at accounts, or delivered volume drifting away from measured draw-down

pros.claim: Stocking only what the room draws removes the most common reason an office quietly starts resenting its coffee vendor
pros.example: pulling an unused flavoured creamer line at the client's request instead of restocking it for another two cycles

cons.claim: Honest quantities mean lower delivered volume in the short run and require a conversation the route would rather skip
cons.example: reducing a cup par by a third after measurement, and explaining the smaller drop to a contact who expected the usual stack

failure_modes: shipping an increased quantity first and disclosing it on the invoice afterwards
leaving trial product on the shelf and treating silence as acceptance
incentivizing drivers on delivered volume so par quietly inflates across the book
acceptance_tests: every par increase and every new item at an account traces to a dated client agreement, and every reduction request appears actioned in the following cycle's record
revisit_triggers: a client questions a delivered quantity or asks for less
delivered volume per account rises without a matching rise in measured draw-down

nodes.definition: Control product age in the three places it hides: the depot shelf, the van, and the client's own cabinet. The practice is first-in-first-out by date code with the oldest usable stock always forward, roast or best-by dates checked at receipt and again at the stop, dairy and refrigerated creamer handled to the storage class its packaging and the local rules require, and an explicit understanding that a parked van in summer is an ageing chamber for coffee, chocolate and creamer. It includes rotating the client's shelf during the stop rather than stacking new product in front of old, pulling and logging expired or damaged stock with a reason rather than quietly discarding it, and treating a recurring rotation finding as evidence that par or cadence is wrong rather than as a housekeeping nuisance.

included: date-code checks at receipt, load and stop
rotation of the client's shelf and van stock
logged disposal and the feedback into par and cadence
excluded: asserting a specific shelf-life or storage-temperature rule as fact rather than a class to verify
credit and billing treatment of discarded product

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: disposal logs or client taste complaints concentrating on particular accounts, items or vehicles

pros.claim: Rotating the client's shelf keeps the cup tasting the way it did during the trial and surfaces par errors early
pros.example: finding a fractional-pack case at the back of the cabinet dated months before the ones just delivered

cons.claim: Rotation adds minutes to every stop and occasionally means carrying stock back off the route
cons.example: unstacking a client's cabinet to bring older cases forward while the driver's next access window is closing

failure_modes: stacking new deliveries in front of older stock so the oldest never moves
leaving chocolate and creamer in a hot van across a long midday break
discarding aged product without logging it, hiding the par error that caused it
acceptance_tests: date codes are recorded at receipt and checked at the stop, disposals are logged with a reason, and any account with a repeat aged-stock finding has a par or cadence change recorded against it
revisit_triggers: a second aged-stock finding at the same account
a seasonal temperature swing or a change of vehicle that alters storage conditions

nodes.definition: Choose how often each account is visited. The constraint is arithmetic: draw-down times cycle length must stay inside the client's storage capacity and inside the freshness window of the fastest-ageing item, while the resulting stop must still fit a repeatable route day. Cadence is the main cost dial of the whole business, because one extra visit per account per month multiplies across the entire book, so it is set from measured draw-down and storage rather than habit, reviewed each cycle, and changed deliberately and visibly rather than allowed to drift. This unit also defines the exception path - what qualifies as an emergency or on-demand stop, who may authorize one, and how those stops are recorded so their true frequency is visible - and schedules the preventive-maintenance tasks that ride along on ordinary stops.

included: cycle-length derivation from draw-down, storage and freshness
the emergency and on-demand stop exception rule
scheduling ride-along preventive maintenance
excluded: whether the resulting stop is profitable and how it should be priced
the geographic assignment of the stop to a day zone

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: logged stock-outs, emergency stops or aged product that contradict the current cycle length

pros.claim: Cadence set from measurement rather than habit is the cheapest lever the operation has, because it multiplies across every account
pros.example: moving a low-draw account with ample storage from weekly to biweekly, freeing a slot on a crowded day

cons.claim: Stretching cadence increases stock-out exposure and forces larger drops the client must house
cons.example: a biweekly cycle at an account with one shelf, where the last three days run on the reserve

failure_modes: stretching cadence past the freshness window of creamer or ground coffee to save a stop
letting emergency stops become an unrecorded second cadence nobody planned or costed
changing cadence without telling the client, so the room budgets its coffee against the old rhythm
acceptance_tests: each account's cadence shows the draw-down, storage cap and freshness window it was derived from, and every emergency stop is logged so the effective cadence is visible
revisit_triggers: a stock-out, an aged-product finding, or a run of emergency stops at the account
a measured change in draw-down or in available storage

nodes.definition: Group accounts into geographic clusters and assign each cluster a repeating day so the week runs the same way every week. Anchor day zones on dense corridors - an office park, a cluster of towers, a medical campus - and interleave cadence classes so weekly, biweekly and monthly accounts share the same zone on alternating weeks rather than scattering across the map. The design objective is stated as a mechanism: raise the share of the day spent inside accounts and lower the share spent in the vehicle, the lobby and the elevator. Density is built rather than found, so new placements are steered toward existing zones and days, and a placement far outside every zone is accepted only with an explicit decision about the day it will damage.

included: clustering accounts into day zones and interleaving cadence classes
the rule for steering new placements toward existing zones
the explicit decision required for an out-of-zone placement
excluded: the profitability of a stop or the value of route density as an asset
day-of-service sequencing inside a zone

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: recorded drive-time and stop-count history per day zone, or a wave of placements and cancellations that shifts density

pros.claim: Repeating day zones convert scattered obligations into a predictable week that a driver can run and a dispatcher can staff
pros.example: one tower cluster serviced every Tuesday, so badge access and dock booking become routine rather than negotiated each visit

cons.claim: Zoning constrains when a client can be served and makes an eagerly promised day expensive to honour
cons.example: a new account in an outlying industrial park that only fits by adding an hour of driving to an otherwise dense day

failure_modes: promising a service day at sale time before the zone map is consulted
letting cadence classes pile onto the same week so one day carries double the stops
keeping a legacy zone that no longer has the density that justified it
acceptance_tests: every account belongs to a named day zone with its cadence class, and any out-of-zone placement carries a recorded decision naming the day it burdens
revisit_triggers: a cluster of new placements or cancellations changes the density of a zone
recorded drive time on a day rises without a matching rise in stops served

nodes.definition: Sequence each day inside the constraints that actually bind an office route rather than inside a map: building access and delivery hours, badge, escort and lobby check-in requirements, freight-elevator bookings, loading-zone availability and the real cost of parking in a dense core, the client's own no-service periods such as an all-hands or a booked boardroom, the morning rush that should be served before or after but not during, and the driver's legal and humane hours including a break. Time windows dominate raw distance optimization, because the shortest path that arrives at a locked suite has produced nothing. The sequence is written down as the day's plan with its hard windows marked, so a disruption can be re-planned against the constraints instead of improvised.

included: ordering stops against access windows, docks and parking
marking hard windows and no-service periods in the day plan
re-planning rules when a stop is blocked
excluded: which accounts belong to the day at all
the cost accounting of the day's minutes

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: aborted-stop records and arrival-time history showing which windows the plan keeps missing

pros.claim: Sequencing to real access windows removes the wasted return trips that quietly consume a route day
pros.example: servicing a badge-access suite immediately after the contact's known arrival rather than at the geographically convenient hour

cons.claim: Window-driven sequencing accepts extra driving and leaves the day fragile to any single delay
cons.example: crossing back through a downtown core at midday because that tenant admits vendors only between ten and eleven

failure_modes: optimizing purely on distance and arriving at closed or unattended suites
ignoring dock and elevator bookings so bottles and cases wait in a lobby
packing the day with no slack, so one equipment failure destroys the rest of it
acceptance_tests: the day plan lists each stop with its hard access window and check-in requirement, and blocked or aborted stops are recorded with the constraint that caused them
revisit_triggers: a building changes its access hours, vendor check-in or dock rules
aborted stops repeat at the same account or the same time of day

nodes.definition: Decide what rides on the van each morning and how it stays under control. The load is built stop by stop from par minus expected on-hand, plus a deliberately sized floating buffer for the surprises a route always produces, arranged so the first stops are nearest the doors and heavy water sits low and secured. It includes the vehicle's weight and volume limits, a shelving or tote system that keeps cases from tumbling into the aisle, the filters, parts and at least one swap unit for the machine classes on that day's route, overnight security of product and equipment, temperature exposure in a parked vehicle, and an end-of-day reconciliation of loaded against delivered against returned that surfaces miscounts and shrink while the day can still be reconstructed.

included: per-stop pick lists and buffer sizing
load arrangement, capacity limits, parts and swap units
end-of-day reconciliation and shrink detection
excluded: depot purchasing and supplier reorder decisions
vehicle financing, insurance or fleet acquisition advice

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: reconciliation variances, buffer exhaustion events, or return volumes that indicate the load rule is mis-sized

pros.claim: A pick-list load with a sized buffer prevents both the second trip and the rolling warehouse a van becomes when everything is carried just in case
pros.example: carrying one spare brewer of the class on that day's route rather than one of every class the fleet owns

cons.claim: Tight load-outs leave no slack for a surprise, and reconciliation adds a task at the end of an already long day
cons.example: arriving at a stop that consumed far more than expected with no reserve cases of that item on board

failure_modes: loading from memory rather than from par minus on-hand
an unreconciled van where shrink and miscounts are indistinguishable
unsecured heavy stock that shifts in transit and injures the driver at the door
acceptance_tests: the day's load traces to a pick list built from par minus on-hand plus a stated buffer, and the end-of-day reconciliation of loaded, delivered and returned closes with variances explained
revisit_triggers: repeated buffer exhaustion or repeated returns of the same item
a change of vehicle, shelving system or route composition

nodes.definition: Keep the depot able to fill tomorrow's pick lists without becoming a graveyard of stale product. Reorder points are derived from route-wide draw-down and the supplier's observed lead time, not from a habit of ordering on a particular weekday; minimum order quantities, freight breaks and volume incentives are weighed against roast-date freshness, storage space and the cash tied up in a pallet of an item the route consumes slowly. Receiving checks the packing list and the date codes before the stock is put away, slotting places fast-moving items nearest the load-out door, cycle counts on a rotating schedule catch drift before an annual count does, and a variance log distinguishes miscount from damage from shrink so the right problem gets fixed.

included: reorder points from draw-down and observed lead time
receiving checks, slotting and rotating cycle counts
the variance log separating miscount, damage and shrink
excluded: supplier negotiation, rebate and cost-of-goods strategy
the price at which product is sold to accounts

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: observed supplier lead-time drift, cycle-count variance patterns, or depot ageing found at receipt

pros.claim: Reorder points tied to observed lead time absorb supplier variability without buying a quarter of stale coffee
pros.example: raising the reorder point on one line after two consecutive late deliveries rather than raising the order size on everything

cons.claim: Freshness-first purchasing forgoes some volume incentives and demands more frequent, smaller orders
cons.example: declining a pallet break on a slow-moving flavoured line that the route would take months to consume

failure_modes: buying to a discount rather than to draw-down and ageing the stock in the depot
putting stock away without checking date codes, so rotation fails at the source
counting only annually, so shrink is discovered long after its cause
acceptance_tests: each stocked line has a reorder point derived from route draw-down and observed lead time, receiving records date codes, and cycle counts close with variances classified
revisit_triggers: supplier lead time or reliability changes
cycle counts show recurring variance on the same lines or slots

nodes.definition: Define the recurring work that keeps equipment producing an acceptable cup and not failing between stops, and attach each task to an interval derived from evidence rather than folklore. The task set spans brew basket, spray head and server or urn cleaning with the correct food-contact chemicals, descaling on an interval derived from the measured hardness and the account's throughput, filter changes driven by volume, grinder hopper and burr cleaning where bean-to-cup is placed, cooler and dispense-point sanitization to the class the equipment and the locally verified obligation register require, hot-tank flushing, and drip-tray and drain checks. Tasks are split into those that ride along on a normal stop and those that need a bench or a longer window, and every completed task is recorded against the machine's serial so the history follows the equipment rather than the account.

included: the task set with intervals derived from water condition and throughput
the split between ride-along and bench work
per-serial completion records
excluded: diagnosing and responding to an actual failure
asserting a specific sanitization interval as a legal requirement rather than a class to verify locally

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: failures or scale findings arriving before the scheduled interval, or a change in verified sanitation obligations

pros.claim: Evidence-derived intervals prevent the failures that turn a planned stop into an emergency detour
pros.example: descaling a high-throughput brewer on hard water more often than the standard schedule, and never seeing its heater fail on route

cons.claim: Preventive work consumes stop minutes and chemicals on machines that would probably have survived the cycle anyway
cons.example: a full grinder clean at a low-volume bean-to-cup account that adds minutes to every visit

failure_modes: running one calendar interval across every account regardless of water or volume
cleaning with the wrong chemical class for a food-contact surface
recording maintenance against the account rather than the serial, so history is lost when the machine moves
acceptance_tests: each placed serial carries a task schedule with intervals justified by water condition and throughput, and completion records exist per serial with dates and the chemicals used
revisit_triggers: a water retest, a throughput change, or scale found earlier than the interval predicted
a change in the locally verified sanitation obligation register

nodes.definition: Build the failure side of the operation: a taxonomy of what actually goes wrong - scale-blocked heaters, pumps, valves and solenoids, leaks and weeping fittings, grinder jams, thermostats, cooler compressors, and user-caused faults such as a mis-seated basket - and a triage rule that decides in the first minutes whether a fault is fixed at the counter, swapped for a bench-ready spare, or the unit retired. Spare-pool sizing is a mechanism, not a number: placements of that class, the observed failure rate from the service log, and bench turnaround time together set how many units must be held, which is another reason fleet standardization pays. The response promise made to accounts must be one the route's geography can actually keep, and every fault is logged against the serial so class-level patterns surface and feed back into equipment selection.

included: failure taxonomy and the fix-versus-swap triage rule
spare-pool sizing mechanism and bench turnaround
per-serial fault logging and class-level pattern detection
excluded: the service-level promise as a commercial or retention commitment
warranty negotiation and manufacturer claim strategy

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the accumulating fault log by class and serial, and measured bench turnaround that changes the spare-pool arithmetic

pros.claim: Swap-and-bench converts an unpredictable roadside repair into a short stop and a controlled workshop task
pros.example: leaving a working spare and taking the faulty brewer back to the bench rather than diagnosing a pump on a client's counter

cons.claim: A spare pool is idle capital and bench time is real labour, both of which scale with how many machine classes the fleet carries
cons.example: holding spares for four brewer classes because four different accounts each wanted something distinctive

failure_modes: attempting a long diagnostic at the counter and destroying the rest of the route day
promising a response time the geography cannot support
swapping units without logging serials, so failure history and the register both drift
acceptance_tests: every fault is logged against a serial with its resolution class, the spare pool per machine class traces to placements, observed failure rate and bench turnaround, and the response promise is checked against actual recorded response times
revisit_triggers: a fault pattern concentrates in one class, one serial or one water condition
recorded response times drift away from the promise

nodes.definition: The route driver is the entire customer experience and the only witness to what happens at the account, so define the standard stop and the person who performs it. A standard stop means checking in the way the building requires, counting and recording what is on the shelf before restocking, rotating stock, restocking to par, cleaning the machine and the station, completing any preventive-maintenance task due on that serial, logging faults and client requests, and leaving the room tidier than it was found. The person requires the training classes named in the locally verified obligation register plus chemical handling, safe lifting, ladder and hot-water practice, and vehicle safety. Conduct is explicit: the driver reports what the room needs, never inflates a drop, never pressures a contact, and escalates anything outside the standard rather than improvising a commitment on the operator's behalf.

included: the standard-stop task sequence and its order
required training classes and safety practice
conduct boundaries including the no-inflation and escalation rules
excluded: selling expansion categories or negotiating anything commercial at the stop
compensation design and route staffing economics

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: stop records or client feedback showing standard-stop steps skipped, or a change in the required training classes

pros.claim: A written standard stop makes service predictable across drivers and makes the resulting records comparable between accounts
pros.example: every driver recording shelf on-hand before restocking, so draw-down is measurable regardless of who ran the route

cons.claim: Standardization constrains an experienced driver's judgement and lengthens the stop with recording tasks
cons.example: requiring an on-hand count at a tiny account where the driver can see at a glance what is needed

failure_modes: restocking before counting, which destroys the draw-down signal for that cycle
letting a required training class lapse and discovering it during an inspection or a building audit
a driver making a commitment about product or scheduling that the operation cannot keep
acceptance_tests: the standard stop is documented in order, each driver's required training classes are current and evidenced, and stop records show the on-hand count taken before restocking
revisit_triggers: a new driver joins or a route changes hands
records show steps of the standard stop being skipped, or a training class approaches expiry

nodes.definition: Capture at every stop the record that lets this subdomain retune itself and that the downstream economics layer consumes: quantities delivered by item, on-hand found before restocking, arrival and departure times, preventive-maintenance tasks completed and filter or descale events by serial, faults observed and their resolution, par changes made with the reason, aged or damaged stock removed, and any client request or complaint. Aggregated across cycles these records are the only honest source of draw-down, service minutes and reliability in the whole business - the numbers that par, cadence, territory design and spare-pool sizing are all derived from. This unit defines the fields, the discipline of recording them at the stop rather than reconstructing them later, and the clean handoff of that data to stop-level profitability, pricing and retention work, which happen elsewhere.

included: the per-stop field set and recording discipline
aggregation into draw-down, service-minute and reliability histories
the handoff contract to stop-level economics and retention work
excluded: computing stop profitability, margin or price changes from the data
using stop data to build an expansion or upsell plan

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: gaps or contradictions found when stop records are aggregated, or a new field the downstream layer requires

pros.claim: Stop records taken at the stop are the only defensible basis for every later decision about par, cadence and equipment
pros.example: settling a dispute about how much coffee an account really uses with three cycles of on-hand and delivered counts

cons.claim: Recording discipline costs minutes at every stop and decays under time pressure unless it is enforced
cons.example: a driver running late reconstructing four stops from memory in the van at the end of the day

failure_modes: recording delivered quantities but not on-hand, leaving draw-down unknowable
reconstructing records after the fact so the numbers look complete but are not real
keeping the data in a form the economics layer cannot consume, so it is re-collected by hand
acceptance_tests: each completed stop carries delivered quantities, on-hand found, arrival and departure times, PM and fault entries by serial, and any par change with its reason, in the agreed handoff format
revisit_triggers: the downstream economics or retention work asks a question the record cannot answer
record completeness drops on a route or a driver

edges.why_related: the survey exists to test whether a room can meet the done-state the mandate defines
placing equipment that handles food-contact product is what creates the obligations the register must name
on-site headcount, room count and observed cup use come from the survey and are the profile's inputs
the survey identifies the exact supply point that must be tested and any building-side treatment already in line
peak demand and drink mix from the profile determine which brewing class can serve the room
the filtration class the water demands changes the cost and viability of a plumbed system against bottles
the machine class fixes the water connection type, pressure need and electrical draw the utilities must supply
choosing plumbed over bottled is what creates the tap, backflow and drainage work in the first place
install day cannot flush, brew and hand over until the utilities are connected and verified
the verified obligation register dictates the sanitizing steps and documentation that install-day sign-off must include
the handover record is where serials, filters and install dates enter the asset register
the placed machine classes decide which coffee formats the catalog is obliged to carry
par is set per catalog item, so the item set must exist before any quantity can be assigned
cycle length is the interval that par must cover, so cadence is derived jointly with the quantity the shelf can hold
rotation and staling control operate on whatever quantity par places on the client's shelf
cadence classes are what the day zones must interleave, so territory design follows the cycle decision
sequencing orders the stops that the zone and day assignment has already fixed
the pick list is par minus expected on-hand, so the load cannot be built before par exists
aggregate load-outs are the demand the depot's reorder points must cover
the sanitization tasks and chemical classes in the maintenance plan come from the locally verified obligation register
what preventive work is done and how well determines which failures the swap process ever has to handle
the driver's required training classes and handling rules are drawn from the obligation register
the record exists only if the standard stop requires counting and logging before restocking
counter space, circuit capacity and water access cap which machine classes are physically possible in that room
the storage volume the survey measured is a hard ceiling on any par regardless of consumption
par may not exceed what measured draw-down supports and what the client has agreed to house
measured hardness and throughput set a floor on descale and filter-change frequency that no schedule may stretch
route density pushes toward fewer, larger visits while service quality and freshness push toward more frequent ones
edges.resolution_rule: storage capacity and the freshness window win: cadence may only be stretched if par still fits the client's storage and stays inside the shortest item's freshness window, otherwise the density problem is solved by re-zoning rather than by starving the account

edges.why_related: raising par is the cheapest way to cut stop frequency and is also the fastest way to leave a client holding stock they never asked for
edges.resolution_rule: the ethics rule dominates: no par increase ships without prior disclosure and agreement, and route cost is instead reduced by cadence, format or zoning changes

edges.why_related: the machine classes that make the best cup are usually the ones that demand the most cleaning minutes and carry the richest failure modes
edges.resolution_rule: place the higher-maintenance class only where the cleaning minutes fit the planned stop and a spare of that class is held; otherwise specify the simpler class and record why

edges.why_related: an emergency swap consumes the slack a sequenced day does not have and pushes stops with hard access windows
edges.resolution_rule: restore a down machine first, then re-plan the day against hard windows: window-bound stops are rescheduled rather than attempted late, and the displaced stops are recorded so the true cost of the emergency is visible

edges.why_related: a deep floating buffer on the van prevents second trips but ages product in a hot vehicle and hides shrink
edges.resolution_rule: cap the buffer at what the route's observed surprises justify and rotate van stock on the same date-code discipline as the depot; when the buffer repeatedly ages out, fix par or cadence instead of enlarging the load

edges.why_related: scale from untreated hard water is the dominant cause of heater, valve and flow failures in placed brewing equipment
connection defects such as piercing valves, crushed lines and shared circuits generate leaks and nuisance faults that present as equipment failure
the rate at which the room draws product is what makes a given cycle length either sufficient or a stock-out
a placement joins a route day only after handover sign-off records the access rules, contact and agreed service day
on-hand and delivered counts from completed stops are the measured draw-down that resets par
stock-outs, aged stock and emergency stops in the record are the evidence that a cycle length is wrong
recovered and refurbished units re-enter the spare pool and their service history informs the triage rule for their class
both are the same reorder arithmetic at different scales: cover expected draw-down over a lead time with a safety allowance, capped by storage and freshness

conflict_axes.name: service_frequency_versus_route_density
conflict_axes.description: Frequent visits keep rooms stocked and product fresh but shred route productivity; stretched cycles buy density at the cost of larger drops and stock-out exposure.
poles: visit more often for freshness and reliability
visit less often for route productivity
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: derive cycle length from measured draw-down against storage and freshness caps, then solve remaining density problems by re-zoning rather than by stretching the cycle past those caps

conflict_axes.name: honest_par_versus_fewer_stops
conflict_axes.description: Larger drops are the cheapest way to remove stops from the route and the fastest way to fill a client's closet with product they never agreed to hold.
poles: stock heavier to reduce visits
stock only what draw-down and agreement support
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat the disclosed, agreed quantity as a hard ceiling and pursue route savings through cadence, format and zoning instead

conflict_axes.name: premium_equipment_versus_serviceability
conflict_axes.description: Bean-to-cup and specialty equipment wins the room's affection but multiplies cleaning minutes, parts, training and spare-pool cost per placement.
poles: place the machine the client will love
place the machine the route can support
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: allow the higher-maintenance class only where planned stop minutes absorb its cleaning and a spare of that class is already held

conflict_axes.name: bottled_versus_plumbed_water
conflict_axes.description: Bottles carry recurring lifting, storage and elevator labour; plumbed systems trade that away for install work, building permission and a standing leak exposure.
poles: bottled simplicity and reversibility
plumbed labour savings with install risk
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: decide from measured water draw, the access path, available storage and a documented building permission, keeping bottled as the explicit fallback when permission is uncertain

conflict_axes.name: sku_variety_versus_inventory_discipline
conflict_axes.description: Variety pleases individual drinkers while every additional item multiplies warehouse slots, truck space, counting time and dead stock.
poles: say yes to the account's product requests
hold a short shared core catalog
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: admit a variable-tail item only with an owning account, a stocking plan and a review date, and retire it when the account or the machine class that justified it leaves

conflict_axes.name: truck_buffer_depth_versus_freshness_and_shrink
conflict_axes.description: A deep rolling buffer rescues surprise stops but ages product in a hot vehicle and makes shrink hard to distinguish from miscount.
poles: carry a deep buffer for resilience
carry a lean pick-list load
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: size the buffer from the route's observed surprise rate, rotate van stock by date code, and reconcile daily so drift is visible

conflict_axes.name: install_speed_versus_verified_compliance
conflict_axes.description: A client who has just signed wants coffee tomorrow, while obligation verification, licensed trade work and water testing all consume calendar days first.
poles: install now and sort the paperwork later
verify obligations and utilities before any install
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep a reversible interim option such as a bottled or countertop placement available while verification completes, and never let it become the permanent unverified install

conflict_axes.name: fix_on_site_versus_swap_and_bench
conflict_axes.description: Repairing at the counter can save a swap unit and a second trip, but it gambles the rest of a sequenced route day on an uncertain diagnosis.
poles: diagnose and repair in place
swap the unit and bench the fault
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: apply a time-boxed triage rule at the counter and swap once the box expires, logging the fault against the serial either way

conflict_axes.name: access_windows_versus_geographic_clustering
conflict_axes.description: Buildings admit vendors when it suits them, which regularly contradicts the tidy geographic order that would minimize driving.
poles: sequence for minimum driving
sequence for guaranteed access
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat hard access windows as fixed points and optimize distance only in the space between them, recording aborted stops so chronic conflicts get re-zoned

conflict_axes.name: driver_autonomy_versus_standardized_recording
conflict_axes.description: An experienced driver's judgement is faster than a checklist, but only a standard stop produces records comparable across accounts and drivers.
poles: let the driver work the room their way
run the standard stop and record every field
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the count-before-restock and per-serial logging steps mandatory and leave the rest of the stop to the driver's judgement

edge_cases.description: Building management refuses any new tap into the supply, or requires a licensed trade with an insurance certificate and its own permit before a plumbed system may be connected
edge_cases.trigger: the landlord or property manager reviews the plumbed water proposal after the survey
edge_cases.mitigation: hold a bottled or countertop fallback specification ready, obtain the building's written conditions before scheduling any trade work, and record the refusal against the account so it is not re-proposed each year

edge_cases.description: The water test comes back very hard or heavily treated, so filters exhaust and scale forms far faster than the standard interval assumes
edge_cases.trigger: a dated test at the actual supply point, or scale found on a machine well before its scheduled descale
edge_cases.mitigation: shorten filter and descale intervals for that serial, add a scale-inhibition stage where the class permits, and flag the account as a candidate for a more tolerant machine class

edge_cases.description: The client shifts to a hybrid schedule and on-site headcount collapses, leaving par far above what the room now draws
edge_cases.trigger: a return-to-office or hybrid policy change, or two consecutive cycles of falling draw-down
edge_cases.mitigation: rebuild the consumption profile from the new pattern, cut par and cadence proactively, remove aged stock, and tell the client the reduction rather than waiting to be asked

edge_cases.description: Stock is kept in a shared janitorial closet and quantities disappear between visits, so measured draw-down overstates real consumption
edge_cases.trigger: on-hand counts that fall faster than the room's observed use, or the client reporting missing product
edge_cases.mitigation: move stock to a lockable location agreed with the contact, log the variance separately from consumption, and avoid raising par to cover unexplained loss

edge_cases.description: A machine fails at a high-visibility account on a Monday and no spare of that class is on the van or in the pool
edge_cases.trigger: a fault call on a class the fleet holds only one or no spare of
